title: Decoder floors: universality, projection transfer and batching reductions; C(P112) ≥ 64 reduced to named conjectures, C(P120) ≥ 72 restated on N₀ (no κ claim)
body:
Research note, no κ claim. Adds `research/decoder-floors-reduction/` only; `bash verify.sh` re-runs every check (about 6 min, ≤ 3 processes, numpy only, no SAT solver).

## Target

philippeVV's gain law (#1587, follow-up 6): `gain(L) = |L| − C(L)` is monotone and superadditive, so "decoder optimisation is dead" for every E8 line set is the single statement **C(P120) ≥ 72** (gain ≤ 48).
It implies P112 ≥ 64, P111 ≥ 63 and P104 ≥ 56. The converse does not follow (P112 ≥ 64 does not imply P120 ≥ 72). philippeVV's follow-up 8 closes all lift cases and names R1–R4.

## New results in this PR

1. **Universality (PROVEN, any E8 line set with the dense table).** Every decoder of every masked realisation becomes a decoder of the single matrix `N₀ = G/2` at the same cost, by adding cost-0 single-entry terms on non-orthogonal pairs. So `C(L)` is the minimum over decoders of `N₀(L)`. The inside / one-sided / two-sided split of `N₀` is exhaustive, and the rank of a realisation is not an invariant. This is a full-class statement, so it survives the gain-law padding.
2. **Structure (PROVEN, any line set).** The outside factors of a two-sided decoder are free. Sylvester gives `m ≥ 10`, and `m = 10` forces `(s,t) = (1,1)`. In the Lemma-D normal form `|J_Q| ≥ t + 2`.
3. **P112 two-sided decoders.**
   - Projection transfer: `cost(P,Q) = cost(P,Q_H) − Σ_{J_Q} ε^col` with `(P,Q_H)` one-sided. Only outside corrections are new.
   - Pivot bound (CONDITIONAL on #2816 R4).
   - `m = 10` with a 2-element circuit is closed (via #2724 and #2338).
   - CHECKED catalogue of outside-column corrections (511 classes × 1200 directions).
   - For `t = 1`: pair lemma, low-column collinearity, at most two weight-7 columns, and an exact saving count. **The disjoint `(1,1)`, `m = 10` case is closed** (`E_Q, E_P ≤ 8`, so `E_Q + E_P ≤ 16 < 17`; idempotent-rank and Ω-orthonormality argument, CHECKED `d4.py`, `omega.py`).
   - Items 3.x depend on the open PRs #2724 / #2816 and are labelled CONDITIONAL on them.
4. **Batching reduces to the single-call floor.**
   - Multiplicity inequality and converse.
   - Twin-fold theorem TF (proportional shared terms never help).
   - Transport lemma: twins are the only cost-monotone line-wise folds.
   - Fold barrier: rank-(2,2) multi-diagonal terms survive every fold.
   - Relative-rank lemma and free dangling.
   - Covering ceiling of 9 per block.
   - Lemma K′ and Lemma E: the GL(9) digon clique costs ≥ 64k + 7.
   - Theorems C, D and M.
   - Dangling-proof witness bound: one shared term with square coordinate restrictions is closed unconditionally in **277/512** (pair, chart) cases (CHECKED on 8 charts).

## Conjectures (the remaining gaps)

Decoder optimisation is dead on every slice above, modulo the open PRs cited. On P112, K1 ∧ K2 ⇒ `C(P112) ≥ 64` (with #2338; CONDITIONAL on #2816). On P120 the master is only **restated** on `N₀`: the route needs #2338's inside floor on P120, K4 and a two-sided P120 analogue of K1.

- **K-P120 (master).** Every decoder of `N₀(P120)` costs ≥ 72. By universality this *is* `C(P120) ≥ 72`, restated rather than reduced.
- **K1.** Every two-sided decoder of `N₀(P112)` costs ≥ 64. Equivalently, outside corrections never exceed the excess of the one-sided projection. K1 ∧ K2 ⇒ `C(P112) ≥ 64` (CONDITIONAL on #2816).
- **K2.** One-sided excess pays for corrections: `Δ ≥ n_nf` for `n_nf ≥ 3` (#2816, #2826).
- **K3.** `(1,1)`, `m = 10`, non-disjoint `|J_P ∩ J_Q| ≥ 2`: cost ≥ 64 (the disjoint case is closed here).
- **K4.** P120 versions of the one-sided results, and P112 certification of #2819.
- **K5 (batching, H×).** A single-call decoder containing a cancelled residual costs ≥ 64 + 7.
- **K6.** A per-term floor for label windows h ≥ 12 (break-even 51 / 46 / 42 at h = 12 / 13 / 14 is recorded pricing, not re-run). The full master over all tables also needs h = 10, 11 (#2639) and K6; #2639's per-term floors are not by themselves shown to give 72 on P120.

**Relation to philippeVV's R1–R4 (#1587 follow-up 8).**
- R1 and R2 are not needed for the master: universality replaces every realisation by `N₀`. Universality does not prove R1 or R2. R2 is #1212.
- R4's `m ≥ 10` part is K-P120; its P112 shadow is K1 ∧ K2, and its first open configuration is K3 (non-disjoint). R4's `h ≥ 10` part is #2639 plus K6.
- R3 is not addressed here.
